about: Where Google, Amazon (and AWS) and Microsoft stand among the companies in the newsroom's data, from public pages other than websummit.com. On 11 November 2026 whatever rested only on websummit.com (its partners list, its speakers page, its press releases and posts) was taken off; those cells say so, and each comes back when another public source we may read carries it. Each remaining cell is one relation to one centre with one state: found (with its source), searched and not found, taken off, or not looked at yet. By dev.graphs@PrompTugal.dinis.

builton.label: 3 of 14 read
builton.text: Of the 14 companies' own pages read, three name Google Cloud: Elastic (on its cloud marketplace), Datadog (a monitoring product page; no partnership claimed) and ManageEngine (cloud security for Azure, AWS and GCP as a product area; coverage, not a partnership). Fourteen of the 17 other companies in the newsroom's data have now had their front page read (researcher@, batches 1 and 2); three (Akamai, Genspark, PitchBook) refuse a plain fetch and are not read. A page not showing something does not mean the tie is absent. A menu link, a customer story or a rival comparison is not a partnership, and each line says which it is.

builton.label: 11 of 17 sell on AWS Marketplace
builton.text: Two lenses. Front pages (14 of the 17 other companies in the newsroom's data read): five name AWS, in different ways: Cerebras (a testimonial by an AWS vice president on a joint inference setup, not called a partnership), Elastic (on its cloud marketplace), Datadog (a monitoring product page, no partnership claimed), ManageEngine (product coverage) and Runpod (a customer compares AWS as the more expensive rival). AWS Marketplace search by company name (all 17, first results only): 11 have a listing of their own, nine under their own name (1Password, Akamai, Cerebras, Datadog, Elastic, IBM, Runpod, Twilio, VTEX) and two under a parent (Cisco for Cisco Outshift, Zoho for ManageEngine); several hold an AWS Specialization badge. A listing shows the company sells there; it is not a stated partnership. A front page understates the tie (Twilio and VTEX said nothing on theirs yet both sell there), so the marketplace is the better first source. Not found in the first results: Mozilla, Gcore, Genspark, KPMG and PitchBook, and the search is fuzzy, so that is not proof of none. Delinea appears only through resellers. The Google Cloud and Microsoft marketplaces could not be read (one shows nothing without interaction, the other refuses automated readers), so only AWS has a marketplace lens.

builton.text: Of the 14 companies' own pages read, six name Microsoft or Azure, in different ways: Elastic (on its cloud marketplace), Datadog (a monitoring product page, no partnership claimed), ManageEngine (product coverage), Gcore (Microsoft quoted as a customer of its CDN), KPMG Portugal (a stated alliance with Microsoft on its own page, headed 'KPMG e Microsoft': it names Azure, Azure OpenAI, Fabric, Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 and Security, and says Microsoft awarded KPMG a supplier-of-the-year prize; the year and category are not on the part read; the strongest tie found) and Delinea (a comparison page against Microsoft, a rival). Fourteen of the 17 other companies in the newsroom's data have now had their front page read (researcher@, batches 1 and 2); three (Akamai, Genspark, PitchBook) refuse a plain fetch and are not read. A page not showing something does not mean the tie is absent. A menu link, a customer story or a rival comparison is not a partnership, and each line says which it is.

past.label: Sines, Nov 2025
past.text: Start Campus, the operator of the Sines data centre campus in Portugal, reported on 11 November 2025 an announcement by Microsoft of USD 10 billion for that campus, after remarks by Microsoft's president at the opening of Web Summit Lisbon: Microsoft's largest Portugal announcement, made in Web Summit week. Portugal's trade agency AICEP also records it (Portugalglobal, 11 December 2025). Microsoft's own page was not read, so he is not described here as a listed speaker, and no stage or time is given. Nscale's releases (15 October 2025, 5 May 2026) describe the deliveries to Microsoft at that campus; its own spending is a different figure from Microsoft's USD 10 billion. The relation is 'announced at the summit's opening', which is neither a partner nor an exhibitor nor a speaker's employer.
